statement: A courier charges $C(w)$ dollars to ship a package that weighs $w$ pounds, where $$C(w) = \begin{cases} 8 & \text{if } 0 < w \le 2 \\ 8 + 3(w - 2) & \text{if } 2 < w \le 10 \\ 32 + 2(w - 10) & \text{if } w > 10 \end{cases}$$ A customer paid $\$41$ to ship one package. How many pounds did the package weigh?

choices.misconception: I solved 32 + 2(w - 10) = 41 as far as w - 10 = 4.5 and then forgot to add the 10 back.
I used the middle rule, 8 + 3(w - 2) = 41, and got 13 without checking that 13 is outside that rule's interval, which ends at 10.
I saw that 41 is 9 dollars more than 32 and added 9 pounds to 10, forgetting that each pound over 10 costs 2 dollars.

hints: First decide which piece of the function can produce a charge of $41$ dollars.
The middle piece reaches at most $C(10) = 32$, so a $41$-dollar charge must come from the last piece.

solutions.reliable: The first piece always gives $8$, and the middle piece rises from $8$ to $C(10) = 8 + 3(8) = 32$. So a charge of $41$ must come from the last piece: $32 + 2(w - 10) = 41$, so $2(w - 10) = 9$, $w - 10 = 4.5$ and $w = 14.5$ pounds. Check: $14.5 > 10$, as that piece requires.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
